author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing treats a page number below the first as the first page
summary: Asking the owner listing for a page number below the first shows the first page as a normal listing instead of the error page.
acceptance_criteria: given the owner listing, when page 0 is requested, then the first page of owners is shown as a normal listing with a success response, not the error page
given the owner listing, when a negative page number is requested, then the first page of owners is shown as a normal listing with a success response, not the error page
given a listing that fits on one page, when a page number below the first is requested, then that listing is shown as normal
given the owner listing, when the first page or a later valid page is requested, then the behavior is unchanged
non_goals: behavior for a page number beyond the last page
behavior for a page value that is not a number
notes: Scope is bounded by the owner's quoted words: "any page value below 1". The unstated neighbours (a page beyond the last, a non-numeric page value, and the veterinarian directory's paging) are recorded as Open Questions in docs/prd.md rather than decided here. No Non-Goals row is touched, so no scope_overrides apply. PRD entry added to the Owner records section with anchor req-ownerspageparam-001, one Done-when bullet, and edge case 4.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Existing owner-paging pattern with one boundary adjustment. OwnerController.processFindForm binds the page request parameter and hands it to findPaginatedForOwnersLastName, which builds a zero-based PageRequest by subtracting one; a value below 1 makes that construction throw and the error page renders. The adjustment normalizes the parameter once at the controller entry, before both the repository call and addPaginationModel. No new type, package, or pattern; the feature-package layout (system-design.md#package-structure) and the Contracts row for OwnerController already carry this surface. That row now names REQ-OWNERSPAGEPARAM-001 and states the guarantee.
integration_points: OwnerController.processFindForm: normalize the bound page value to at least the first page before it is used

OwnerController.addPaginationModel: the currentPage model attribute must carry the normalized value, since ownersList.html derives the first/previous/next/last links and the current-page marker from it
OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith: unchanged; it receives a Pageable whose page index is now always valid

patterns.description: findPaginatedForOwnersLastName is the one place converting the one-based request page to a zero-based PageRequest; normalize upstream of it rather than inside, so the view model and the query see the same page number
MockMvc listing test shape: stub findByLastNameStartingWith with a PageImpl, GET /owners with the page parameter, assert status and view name

risks.risk: Normalizing inside the pagination helper only would leave currentPage at the raw value; ownersList.html would then render a previous link to a page below the first and fail to mark the current page
risks.mitigation: Normalize once in processFindForm and pass the normalized value to both the helper and addPaginationModel

risks.risk: The one-page acceptance criterion is invisible if the stubbed page holds exactly one owner: processFindForm redirects to the owner detail on a single total element, so the test would assert the redirect rather than the listing
risks.mitigation: Stub the single-page case with more than one owner and assert the owners/ownersList view with a success status

risks.risk: Reviewers may read the clamp as a business rule added to a controller, which architecture-principles.md forbids in the Web controller row
risks.mitigation: It is request adaptation, not a domain rule: the parameter is normalized at the HTTP binding boundary and no owner-domain invariant moves into the controller

notes: Trust boundary: security-principles.md § Trust Boundaries requires external input validated for range before use. The product contract for this parameter now admits any integer and defines values below the first as the first page, so normalization at the boundary satisfies the rule; rejection is not the required response. The change also removes an unhandled IllegalArgumentException reaching the error page, which narrows the internal-detail exposure recorded as a Known Defect for REQ-SYS-002 without addressing that defect. Non-goals stand: a page beyond the last page still yields an empty result handled by the existing not-found branch, a non-numeric page value still fails binding, and VetController keeps its own independent paging helper - both are Open Questions in docs/prd.md and must not be touched by this slice. No ADR: the decision is neither hard to reverse nor a trade-off. Durable memory written: docs/system-design.md Contracts row for OwnerController gains the guarantee sentence and the requirement id (contracts-sync passes). No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty.

A reader who sees `requestedPage` passed to `findPaginatedForOwnersLastName` and `addPaginationModel` has to reread the clamp line to learn it is not the raw request value; architecture-principles.md's naming principle requires the name alone (not the body) to answer what a unit holds.
findings.fix: Rename `requestedPage` to something that names the clamp outcome, e.g. `effectivePage` or `normalizedPage`.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: theOwnerListingShouldShowTheOnlyPageWhenThePageNumberIsBelowTheFirst only exercises page=0. The sibling multi-page test parameterizes {0, -3}, and prd.md edge case 4 states the rule holds 'whether or not the listing runs beyond one page' — the negative-page value is untested for the single-page scenario, so acceptance criterion 3 (a listing that fits on one page, with a page number below the first) is only partially covered.
findings.fix: Change the method to @ParameterizedTest with @ValueSource(ints = { 0, -3 }) (reusing the pageBelowTheFirst parameter name from the sibling test) so both boundary values are covered for the single-page case too.

findings.description: totalOwners = 12 is a bare literal whose only real constraint is 'more than one page' (i.e. greater than PAGE_SIZE). Per testing-principles.md Derived Expectations, a value chosen to satisfy a condition should be expressed as that condition rather than a magic number.
findings.fix: Replace `int totalOwners = 12;` with a value derived from PAGE_SIZE, e.g. `int totalOwners = PAGE_SIZE + 1;`, so the reader sees why the count produces more than one page.

recommendations: The added rule (int requestedPage = Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE);) is pure, branchless logic that could be unit-tested without booting MockMvc/Spring context, per testing-principles.md's pyramid guidance ('could this have been tested without booting the framework?'). Given its triviality and that the two new MockMvc tests already verify the end-to-end behavior (status 200, correct view, currentPage model attribute) rather than just the clamp, this is not blocking, but a future controller-side rule of any complexity should get an isolated unit test first.
approved_aspects: New tests avoid the totalElements()==1 redirect trap correctly (2 owners in the single-page fixture), matching the risk the design-block flagged

Both new tests are real end-to-end proof of the fix: since PageRequest.of(page-1, pageSize) throws for page<=0 pre-fix, the request succeeding with HTTP 200 is genuine evidence of the fix rather than an artifact of mocking
Test names follow the theSubjectShouldOutcome BDD school and read as specifications
Four-phase structure (arrange/act/assert) with blank-line separation, no phase comments, consistent with the file's existing MockMvc idiom
Uses the existing george()/PageImpl fixtures and FIRST_PAGE/PAGE_SIZE constants rather than inventing new scaffolding
Full test suite passes (./gradlew test), including the new tests

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain not verified against the NVD in this review: the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle (plugins are java, checkstyle, jacoco, spring-boot 4.1.0, dependency-management 1.1.7, graalvm native 1.1.2, cyclonedx 3.2.4, javaformat 0.0.47), and this reviewer has no network access. Spring Boot 4.1.0 governs the managed versions. The build does produce a CycloneDX SBOM, so a human or CI can close the CVE check from it. No dependency changed in this slice, so the check is unchanged-from-baseline rather than newly at risk.

VetController.java:61 holds the same PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize) construction with no clamp, so a page below the first there still throws into the error page. This is the pre-existing baseline, is recorded as an Open Question in docs/prd.md, and is explicitly out of this slice's scope — noted only so the class is not lost, not as a finding against this change.
approved_aspects: Boundary validation: the request-bound page parameter is normalized once at the HTTP boundary in OwnerController.processFindForm (Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE)) before it reaches either the repository call or the view model, matching security-principles.md § Trust Boundaries (validate range before use). No path leaves the raw value in scope: both usages take effectivePage.

No new vulnerability class from security-principles.md § Realization is introduced. Data access still runs through the derived repository query with a Pageable (no concatenated query text); no template escaping is disabled; no request-derived value composes a path or resource name; no binder or bound type changes, so the mass-assignment posture is untouched; no endpoint, route, or management exposure is added.

Integer handling is safe at both extremes: Math.max(page, 1) makes page - FIRST_PAGE non-negative for every int input including Integer.MIN_VALUE, so no underflow reaches PageRequest.of. Page size stays a fixed constant (5), so a request-supplied value cannot drive allocation size — no unbounded-memory path.

The change strictly narrows exposure relative to the baseline: the previously unhandled IllegalArgumentException from PageRequest.of no longer reaches the error page, which renders the underlying exception message (the internal-detail leak recorded as a Known Defect for REQ-SYS-002). Behavior for valid pages is unchanged.

Model integrity: currentPage now carries the normalized value, so ownersList.html cannot render a first/previous link pointing below the first page — the view no longer derives navigation from an out-of-range request value.

No secrets, credentials, tokens, or connection strings appear anywhere in the diff; no logging statement is added, so no log-injection or sensitive-data-in-logs surface. No shell execution, deserialization, XML parsing, file I/O, reflection, or randomness is introduced.

Supply chain unchanged: build.gradle is not in the change set and no dependency, repository, or plugin declaration is touched. Test-only additions (junit-jupiter-params, PageRequest) resolve from the existing spring-boot-starter-test.
Test additions are non-production and introduce no security surface; they assert the normalized currentPage, which is the model attribute the view trusts.

author: change-grader
summary: clamp the owner listing page parameter to the first page

blast_radius.note: One module and one method: three effective production lines in OwnerController.processFindForm plus a FIRST_PAGE constant, with the other hunks split between the new tests and two doc records. No sensitive paths, no new dependency, no signature or schema change, and the only affected route is GET /owners.

semantic_surprise.note: Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) is exactly what the requirement asks for, and reading both call sites confirms the normalized value reaches the repository query and addPaginationModel alike, so the rendered currentPage and the fetched page agree and the view's previous/next links cannot point below the first page. The page minus FIRST_PAGE substitution in findPaginatedForOwnersLastName is a literal-for-constant swap with identical arithmetic. Pages past the last and non-numeric values behave exactly as before, and the PRD records both as open questions rather than silently changing them.

test_adequacy.note: Two parameterized MockMvc tests cover page 0 and page -3 across both the multi-page and single-page listings, asserting HTTP 200, the ownersList view, and currentPage 1. They are genuine rather than tautological: before the fix PageRequest.of(-1, 5) throws before the stubbed repository is ever reached, so a green run is real evidence. The single-page fixture holds two owners, which correctly dodges the single-result redirect. The one gap is that no test captures the Pageable to assert the repository received index 0, so the query index is verified only indirectly through the model attribute.

reviewer_hedging.note: All three planned roster reviewers approved in round two with zero findings and zero recommendations, after a round-one changes_requested from code-quality and test that raised only autofix-severity naming and legibility items, all of which are visibly applied in the diff. scope_deviation.note: Zero design revisions, zero consultations, zero build retries, and the diff matches the triaged surface named by the design-block. The PRD edits stay tied to recording the requirement: the new requirement sentence, its acceptance criterion, edge case 4, and two open questions, plus a correction of the now-stale open-question count from ten to five, which I verified against the section (five unstruck questions remain).
